description: I’m a Physics and Science teacher at the Canadian School of Tashkent, passionate about space science and using NASA data to solve local challenges. I welcome motivated teammates with skills in coding, science, data, design, research, or communication. Let’s collaborate and create a solution that makes a difference!
summary:
Sho'r Radar is a decision-support tool for farmers in Uzbekistan, delivered as a Telegram bot and a Telegram Mini App with a map dashboard, in Uzbek, Russian and English. It turns NASA POWER satellite-derived data (root-zone soil wetness, temperature, rainfall, solar radiation) and Open-Meteo forecasts into a clear daily signal: irrigate, monitor or wait. It also gives a salt-risk indicator, qualified flush-timing guidance, and salt-tolerant crop and rotation suggestions based on FAO tables.
Soil salinity and water scarcity threaten yields across Uzbekistan, especially in Karakalpakstan, Bukhara and Syrdarya. Most smallholders have no access to soil sensors or agronomic advice. Sho'r Radar needs only a phone, and farmers can add their own salinity measurements and irrigation logs to sharpen the advice.
It matters because it makes NASA Earth data usable at field level, helping farmers save water, slow salt build-up and protect income. It is honest about its limits. It scores conditions that favour salt rather than measuring salt, and its thresholds are labelled as placeholders until an agronomist reviews them.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS
Sho'r Radar gives farmers in Uzbekistan a daily recommendation: irrigate, monitor or wait. It also gives a salt-risk indicator, qualified guidance on when to flush the soil, and salt-tolerant crop suggestions. Farmers use it through a Telegram bot or a Telegram Mini App with a map dashboard, in Uzbek, Russian and English.

The app pulls NASA POWER data (root-zone soil wetness, temperature, rainfall, humidity, solar radiation) and a 7-day forecast from Open-Meteo. It calculates evapotranspiration with the Hargreaves-Samani method and runs a water balance against crop-specific rules. A salt-risk score combines conditions that favour salt build-up. Crop fit uses FAO salt-tolerance tables. Farmers can add their own field details, soil salinity (ECe) readings, irrigation-water EC, and irrigation and flush logs. A measurement replaces the estimate, and logging an irrigation resets the water deficit. The map shows districts and fields coloured by signal, with NASA GIBS true-colour and MODIS NDVI layers. Every decision has a "How was this decided?" explanation, and all thresholds are in one visible, versioned rules file.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Smallholders without soil sensors or agronomists get timely, plain-language advice on a phone they already own. The aim is to save water, slow salinisation, protect yields and income, and make NASA Earth data usable at field level.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY
Languages and frameworks: Python, FastAPI, aiogram (Telegram bot), SQLite, Leaflet (maps), HTML/JS front end.
Data: NASA POWER, NASA GIBS and MODIS NDVI, Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap.
Deployment: Docker and Render, with a Cloudflare tunnel for testing.
Testing: pytest, including a simulated full bot conversation and a check that every text string exists in all three languages.
Methods: FAO-56, FAO Paper 29 and Maas & Hoffman salt-tolerance tables.
AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) helped with planning, code and draft translations. The team reviewed all outputs.

CREATIVITY
- It uses the channel farmers already use, Telegram, so there is nothing to install.
- It turns satellite data into one decision, not a dashboard of numbers.
- It is built around honesty. It says "field salinity not measured" when that's true, and it labels stale data and demo data.
- It works through outages: NASA data is cached on disk, and the page falls back to the last data saved on the phone.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
- Limits: The NASA grid is about 50 km, so neighbouring fields look alike. Salt is scored from conditions, not measured.
- Thresholds: They are generic placeholders pending agronomist review. Our consistency check on real NASA data confirms the signals move the right way in dry and wet periods, but it is not field validation.
- Safety and privacy: Mini App calls are verified with Telegram's signed login data, users can only access their own data, and they can delete their account. Community posts have report-and-hide moderation.
- Language: The Uzbek and Russian texts need native-speaker review.
